LESSON: READING FOR COMPREHENSION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: GERMAN
Strand: READING Theme 7. My Body
Topic 2.7: Reading for comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading for comprehension, part of READING Theme 7. My Body in Grade 4 GERMAN.

Key inquiry question: Why do you like reading?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify specific vocabulary for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read texts for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. read texts for enjoyment.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading for comprehension in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify specific vocabulary for comprehension,

   Reading for comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read texts for comprehension,

   Reading for comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. read texts for enjoyment.

   Reading for comprehension helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read out body parts from charts/flash cards with peers in plenary,

2. match pictures of body parts with their names,

3. read simple brief poems/texts on body parts and answer given questions.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read out body parts from charts/flash cards with peers in plenary,
2. match pictures of body parts with their names,
3. read simple brief poems/texts on body parts and answer given questions.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading for comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Self-efficacy: The learner develops self-awareness as they read out body parts from charts/flash cards with peers in

plenary.

The learner links the concept of body parts to the same concept in Science and Technology.
